$comment: Guy Inchbald's stellation lists, transcribed from
https://www.steelpillow.com/polyhedra/icosa/printouts.html
read on 16 August 2026.
They are the output of a program he wrote in SAM BASIC, printed on a
dot-matrix printer and later OCR'd; the page says so, and it shows. Each
list applies a different set of acceptance rules to the same arrangement,
so together they show how much of 'the 59' is the rules rather than the
geometry.
`code` is the authority here, not `symbol`. It is a bit per cell type --
1 a, 2 b, 4 c, 8 d, 16 e1, 32 e2, 64 f1 one hand, 128 f1 other hand,
256 f2, 512 g1, 1024 g2, 2048 h -- so it says exactly which cells the
figure holds, while the printed symbol is prose about it and can be (and
in one case is) mistyped. make-icosahedra-rules.mjs regenerates every
symbol from its code and checks it against the printed one.
Two entries are marked `reconstructed`. The fifth list prints '50
icosahedra found' but only 48 rows survive, and its heading is visibly
damaged ('No enanti(omorphs'), so two rows were lost. They can only be
2047 and 4095: this list's rules are those of the fourth list minus one
condition, so it must contain everything the fourth does, and the fourth
ends with those two.

sets.title: The 59 icosahedra
sets.blurb: Miller's rules as Coxeter, Du Val, Flather and Petrie applied them — the canonical list.

sets.title: The 59, with continuous face planes
sets.blurb: The canonical rules with one more: a face plane may not be broken. It removes 25 of the 59.

sets.title: Continuous faces instead of rule (v)
sets.blurb: Drop the ban on separated shells and require continuous face planes in its place. Two figures the canonical list rejects come back.

sets.title: The 59, with continuous edges
sets.blurb: The canonical rules plus a ban on segmented edges — the harshest cut of the canonical list, leaving 25.

sets.title: Continuous edges instead of rule (v)
sets.blurb: Drop the ban on separated shells and require unsegmented edges instead. This is the one set that admits figures far outside the 59 — shells floating free of the core.

sets.title: The 59, with continuous faces and edges
sets.blurb: Both continuity rules on top of the canonical ones. It happens to select the same 25 as the edge rule alone.

sets.title: Continuous faces and edges instead of rule (v)
sets.blurb: Both continuity rules, with the ban on separated shells dropped. Two more than the subset above.
